analytical_dimensions.description: Separate institutional authority and individual views
probing_questions: Identify publishing, commissioning, organizing and hosting relationships from supplied originals or retained provenance. Distinguish an adopted institutional statement, staff/fellow signed contribution, guest view, host question and event participant. Preserve author-views disclaimers and evidence of institutional adoption. An institution hosting a debate is not endorsing every speaker. An external CDN or video can be institutional material if the publishing relationship is established; directory membership or a platform domain alone is insufficient.

Reconstruct each source's problem definition, causal assumptions, affected groups, proposed interventions, normative commitments and strongest counterargument. Compare changes and internal disagreement before generalizing across an institution. Ask which alternatives and interests the text considers or brackets; mark inferences and do not fabricate motives. Funding or affiliation does not establish a position or invalidate an argument. Distinguish no search result, unread material, missing text and an explicit refusal to take a position. Preserve the actual institutional/geographic/language coverage and avoid manufacturing consensus from duplicates or selection bias.

engine_name: Read institutional arguments, authority and framing
problematique: Analyze arguments published or hosted by institutions without collapsing them into a single institutional belief. Establish authority to speak, reconstruct mechanisms and policy commitments, compare internal and external disagreement, and examine what the framing makes visible or leaves unresolved. Evaluate arguments on their evidence while treating affiliation and funding as relationships requiring evidence and an explanatory warrant.
researcher_question: Read institutional arguments, authority and framing
